verses.text: God blessed Noah and his sons and told them, "Have children, multiply, and fill the earth.
Every animal on earth and every bird in the sky will fear you. Everything that moves on the ground, along with every fish in the sea, is handed over to you.
Every living thing that moves can be food for you. Just as I gave you green plants, I'm giving you everything.
But don't eat meat with its life still in it—that is, its blood.
I will call anyone to account for your lifeblood. I will hold every animal accountable, and I will hold each person accountable for another person's life.
Whoever takes a human life, another human will take their life, because God made humans in his own image.
So have children and multiply. Spread across the earth and fill it."
God also spoke to Noah and his sons who were with him:
"As for me, I'm making my covenant with you and with your descendants after you,
and with every living creature that is with you—the birds, the livestock, and every animal on earth that came out of the ark.
I make this covenant with you: never again will all life be wiped out by floodwaters. Never again will a flood destroy the earth."
God said, "Here is the sign of the covenant I'm making between me, you, and every living creature, for all generations:
I've placed my rainbow in the clouds. It will be the sign of my covenant with the earth.
When I bring clouds over the earth and the rainbow appears,
I will remember my covenant between me, you, and every living creature. The waters will never again become a flood that destroys all life.
When the rainbow is in the clouds, I'll see it and remember the lasting covenant between God and every living creature on earth."
God said to Noah, "This is the sign of the covenant I've established between me and every living creature on earth."
Noah's sons who left the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham was the father of Canaan.
These three were Noah's sons, and the whole earth was populated through them.
Noah became a farmer and planted a vineyard.
He drank wine, got drunk, and lay uncovered inside his tent.
Ham, Canaan's father, saw his father uncovered and told his two brothers outside.

Shem and Japheth took a garment and laid it across both their shoulders. They walked backward into the tent and covered their father. They kept their faces turned away, so they didn't see him uncovered.
When Noah sobered up, he learned what his youngest son had done to him.
He said, "Canaan is cursed. He'll be the lowest servant to his brothers."
He also said, "Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Shem. May Canaan serve him.
May God give Japheth more room and let him live in Shem's tents. May Canaan serve them."
Noah lived 350 years after the flood.
Noah lived 950 years altogether, and then he died.
